subject: Harmonic-tier pricing construct for high-volume per-token commitment
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — pricing for sustained 100B tokens/mo

Thanks again for the demo today — the latency profile looked strong.

Quick ask from procurement: we need an example pricing construct for sustained usage at ~100B tokens/month. Specifically:
- A proposal that shows per-token pricing with tiered breakpoints (we want to understand both marginal and blended effective rate examples)
- True-up cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether unused commit can carry forward or convert to credits
- How embeddings are treated — are they charged the same per-token or priced separately?

We have internal constraints around predictable unit economics so the team will push for a structure that limits month-to-month volatility. Attaching the procurement form; forwarding to Tom (legal) for visibility.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — pricing for sustained 100B tokens/mo

Elena — great to meet you virtually. Appreciate the clarity on needs.

High-level response: we can get you a formal commercial proposal, but to make the math simple for procurement I sketched a construct that balances predictability with upside for you as you scale. We call it a "harmonic-tier" construct internally — it’s essentially a tiered per-token ladder where incremental discounts increase for each higher tier but with diminishing incremental change (think harmonic decay instead of linear drops). The goal is to avoid big cliffs while still rewarding committed scale.

Key points:
- Example breakpoints I propose: 10B / 30B / 60B tokens/month (you can shift these).
- Marginal pricing: per-token rate that steps down at each breakpoint.
- Blended effective rate: we’ll show a worked example for 100B/month so you can see the blended cost per token vs marginal.
- True-up: monthly with 3-month carryforward credits (carry unused commit forward for up to 3 months, after which it expires).
- Embeddings: typically priced separately due to different unit economics; propose a hybrid: a small per-embedding rate plus a discounted per-token conversion for normalized counts.

I attached a first-pass rate sheet and will have Ben add a worked example with numbers. Is monthly true-up with limited carryforward acceptable as a starting point?

— Marissa
Director, Deals — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_initial_rate_sheet_v1.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.com>, Tom Hale <tom.hale@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jun 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — harmonic-tier construct (worked numbers)

Elena / team — I put a concrete worked example together so procurement can see marginal vs blended. See attached (ACME_Rate_Sheet_v3.xlsx). Summary below (numbers illustrative):

Proposed harmonic-tier per-token rates (USD per 1k tokens):
- Tier A (0–10B): $0.045
- Tier B (10B–30B): $0.032
- Tier C (30B–60B): $0.022
- Tier D (>60B): $0.016

If ACME uses exactly 100B tokens in a month, marginal calculation charges the tokens in each bucket at that bucket's rate. Blended (effective) rate is total charged / total tokens. Example:
- Charges = (10B*$0.045) + (20B*$0.032) + (30B*$0.022) + (40B*$0.016) = $450k + $640k + $660k + $640k = $2.39M
- Blended rate = $2.39M / 100B tokens = $0.0239 per 1k tokens

Notes and guardrails:
- Smoothing corridor: if month-to-month usage deviates >30% from commit, we apply a temporary buffer rate for the month to limit extreme swings (this prevents cliff collapses in revenue for Redwood and keeps predictability for ACME).
- True-up: monthly true-up with up to 3 months carryforward credits. Carryforward is applied to future billing before on-demand usage.
- Fallback: on-demand (no commit) rate is $0.060 per 1k tokens; falls back automatically if you exceed committed quantity and no additional committed tranche is agreed.
- Embeddings: charged at $0.005 per 1k embeddings or convertible at an approximate 1:8 token ratio (we can make this explicit in the sheet).

Attachment: ACME_Rate_Sheet_v3.xlsx (contains full table, line-by-line calc and example invoice).

Happy to walk through the sheet live; want to make sure we address procurement's concerns about blending vs marginal math.

— Ben
VP, Commercials — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood demo — harmonic-tier construct (worked numbers)

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A couple clarifying asks from procurement:
1) Can the first breakpoint be shifted to 5B instead of 10B (our short-term burst pattern makes the 0–5B bucket relevant)?
2) Do discounts apply to embeddings if they are converted to token-equivalent usage, or do they only get the per-embedding discount?
3) For the smoothing corridor, will you share the exact temporary buffer rate formula we would see if we move outside the 30% band? Procurement likes explicit formulas.

If we can confirm these quickly we can route to legal.

— Elena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tom Hale <tom.hale@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jun 2028 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — harmonic-tier construct (worked numbers)

Elena — quick answers inline: 
1) Breakpoint shift: yes, we can move Tier A to 0–5B and shift the rest (5B / 25B / 60B) — Ben, updated sheet please.
2) Embeddings: we can do a hybrid. Default will be a standalone per-embedding rate (as Ben proposed) but we will include an option to convert embeddings to token equivalents for blended pricing if ACME prefers to consolidate billing. We’ll show both in the commercial.
3) Smoothing buffer formula: if |usage - commit| / commit > 0.30, then buffer_rate = max(on_demand_rate * 0.9, committed_rate * 1.15). The idea is to limit downside while incentivizing predictable behavior. We will state the exact formula in the SOW.

Operational notes:
- Fallback behavior: on-demand fallback at $0.060/1k tokens, automatic for tokens beyond the highest committed tier in any given month unless you buy an additional tranche.
- SLA and billing: we will lock the unit rates for 12 months from signature of the MSA.

Looping in Karthik (solutions) to confirm embeddings conversion math and Tom for legal next steps. Also adding the HubSpot deal link for internal tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2028-RED-042

— Marissa
